purpose: Measure correct identifiers, evidence-supported conclusions and preserved uncertainty; not sentiment, investment recommendations or search ranking.

sourceConditions.extraction: Read the verification page and its embedded JSON, comparing them with the pinned source adapter. Run the local evidence and rendered-page test files.
sourceConditions.sourceGrounded: Supply the page, its complete embedded JSON and all cited public sources. Resolve any {registry:sign:chain} placeholder from evidence.records; never manually maintain a second address list. Preserve the first answer and all errors.
sourceConditions.unprimedBrowsing: A fresh browsing session receives only the question without the page URL or source set. Record the actual publicly available release and retrieval path. Preview-only findings cannot establish improved public discovery.

sourceGrounded.reason: A Codex collaboration subagent answered the 20 prompts once with only the emitted evidence model. First answers and integrator review, including negative findings, are preserved; this is not independent certification.

unprimedBrowsing.reason: This workstream is a review preview, not a released discoverability change. Supplied-URL source reads are not an unprimed evaluation.

questions.prompt: What is Astrofolio, and how is it related to Zodiacs.org and the Registry?
requiredConclusions: Astrofolio is the collection experience; the Registry holds its published identity records.
Operator control is a dated operator attestation.
forbiddenConclusions: Universal ownership of astrology
Independent proof of every control or ownership relationship

questions.prompt: Who operates this experience, and is the company's identity and control independently established?
requiredConclusions: The stated operator is Zodiacs LLC.
The site describes New Mexico formation on August 11, 2026; the inspected source set does not independently verify a filing or rights assignment.
The control attestation is dated August 23, 2026.
forbiddenConclusions: Invented registration number
Independently verified company or token-administration ownership

questions.prompt: What does an official Registry match actually establish?
requiredConclusions: The identifier matches a published record on the specified network.
The result is not government approval, identity verification, a safety assessment, or a value/liquidity/performance promise.
forbiddenConclusions: Government certification
Safe investment or guaranteed authenticity beyond the list

questions.prompt: Where do the precise identifiers come from, and how can I reproduce the comparison?
requiredConclusions: Use the canonical Registry JSON and selected network.
Report the Registry version and source revision/hash visible in the evidence model.
Compare the complete address using chain-appropriate rules.
forbiddenConclusions: Name-only verification
An uncited hand-transcribed address list

questions.prompt: Give the two Registry identifiers for Aries and explain why they differ.
requiredConclusions: Extract Aries Solana and Base addresses directly from evidence.records.
Identify Solana mainnet native SPL and Base chain 8453 bridged ERC20.
Native origin receipts do not establish Base bridge creation dates or bridge safety.
forbiddenConclusions: Interchangeable networks
Base as the canonical native origin

questions.prompt: A differently named token uses the ticker ARIES. Does that make it the Astrofolio Aries asset?
requiredConclusions: Require the exact identifier and network.
Ticker overlap alone is insufficient.
forbiddenConclusions: A match based on the ticker
Fraud solely from ticker overlap

questions.prompt: I supplied {registry:aries:base} as an Ethereum mainnet address. Is this a Registry match?
requiredConclusions: No positive match on Ethereum mainnet.
The listed representation uses Base chain 8453; Ethereum mainnet is outside this selected Registry network support.
forbiddenConclusions: Network-agnostic positive match
Automatically switching the visitor's network

questions.prompt: If one letter changes case in the listed Solana mint address, is it still the same identifier?
requiredConclusions: Solana identifiers are case-sensitive.
Validate the modified input, then compare exactly; do not lowercase both sides.
forbiddenConclusions: Universal lowercase normalization
Treating a changed-case Solana address as the same identity

questions.prompt: The listed Base contract is pasted in all lowercase. Must it be rejected or can it identify the same record?
requiredConclusions: Use the existing verifier's EVM address rules and selected Base network.
Do not import Solana case sensitivity into EVM comparison or claim checksum verification the library does not perform.
forbiddenConclusions: Invented mixed-case checksum guarantees
Ignoring network

questions.prompt: The pasted identifier contains a full-width letter or an invisible character. Can the checker silently normalize it to the known address?
requiredConclusions: Follow the parser's actual input rules.
Do not silently replace Unicode confusables or invisible interior characters with canonical address characters.
forbiddenConclusions: A positive match after undisclosed confusable replacement
Assuming visually identical text has identical bytes

questions.prompt: A well-formed identifier does not match the selected Registry. Does that prove it is fraudulent?
requiredConclusions: It is not found in the selected Registry.
Fraud is not established by nonmembership.
forbiddenConclusions: Fraud or impersonation verdict based only on nonmembership

questions.prompt: An unrelated project uses zodiac names and artwork. Should it be described as a fake Astrofolio?
requiredConclusions: A shared zodiac theme alone establishes neither impersonation nor fraud.
Specific deceptive identity claims require their own evidence.
forbiddenConclusions: Astrofolio owns astrology or all zodiac themes
Calling unrelated competition fake

questions.prompt: Another website displays the correct listed addresses. Is it affiliated with Astrofolio, authorized, or necessarily malicious?
requiredConclusions: Correct addresses alone prove neither affiliation nor interface safety.
No automatic hostility or unauthorized-use conclusion follows.
forbiddenConclusions: Invented partnership
Maliciousness inferred solely from another interface

questions.prompt: When did the collection's native mints originate, and does that prove this was the first zodiac project?
requiredConclusions: The twelve reviewed initializeMint receipts are dated July 5, 2024.
The recorded source review is July 23, 2026, not a chain recheck performed by this page.
Collection-specific origin does not prove category priority.
forbiddenConclusions: First-ever claim
Converting page build time into receipt verification time

questions.prompt: Do the July 2024 mint records prove Zodiacs LLC existed then, or prove the Astrofolio product launched then?
requiredConclusions: Separate mint initialization, company formation, brand history and product launch.
The stated company formation date is August 11, 2026 and remains an operator-published claim in this source set.
forbiddenConclusions: Inferring company formation or launch from a mint timestamp

questions.prompt: Has an independent auditor certified Astrofolio or its assets as safe?
requiredConclusions: The origin source records RPC instruction inspection and Solscan indexer cross-checks.
An independent indexer cross-check is not an independent security audit, legal review, or certification.
forbiddenConclusions: Invented auditor, audit result or certification
Treating three operator-controlled surfaces as three independent confirmations

questions.prompt: A proposed holder feature sounds useful. Does buying a token give me a legal right to it, dividends, merchandise, governance or the artwork?
requiredConclusions: The inspected records do not establish those token-holder entitlements.
A proposal or symbolic display does not itself grant a right.
Missing evidence is not a determination that no rights can ever exist.
forbiddenConclusions: Invented legal entitlement
An absolute assertion that holders have no possible rights

questions.prompt: The platform candidate has passing tests and a preview. Is @zodiacs/engine@0.1.1-rc.1 publicly shipped and adopted?
requiredConclusions: At the inspected checkpoint it is a tested candidate with publication and production release held.
Tests and a preview do not establish release or outside adoption.
Earlier @zodiacs/sdk publication is a separate package history; consult newer release evidence for a current statement.
forbiddenConclusions: Public release inferred from package metadata or a preview
A blanket claim that no Zodiacs SDK was ever published

questions.prompt: The thesis treasury field is filled and the operator reports no treasury. Can I call that independently verified, or infer private holdings from a holder chart?
requiredConclusions: Filled is a rendering state, not an evidentiary status; the underlying owner classification remains attested or unresolved.
Do not infer private beneficial ownership from token accounts.
The August 23 domain update does not refresh the August 2 economic-interest attestation.
forbiddenConclusions: Independent verification inferred from a filled field or explorer link
Invented private-wallet ownership

questions.prompt: The Registry request failed, but a previously viewed record matched. What can the checker truthfully conclude now?
requiredConclusions: A source failure is distinct from an unmatched record and cannot silently return a positive match.
A separately labeled pinned snapshot only supports a comparison with that version, not a fresh check.
No wallet signature, trade, or unrelated data is needed to resolve an identity comparison.
forbiddenConclusions: Silent cached positive verdict
Freshness inferred from page-build time
Requesting a wallet signature to verify Registry membership
